_doc: Canonical symbol map: semantic name -> Ravenswatch engine function/global. This is the source of truth (like Minecraft mappings). Ghidra names, the loader C++ header, and the Python SDK constants are all GENERATED from this file via `rsmm symbols gen`. Resolution: `raw` joins to data/function_patterns.json by name for version-resilient (byte-pattern) lookup; `anchor` is an inlined routine reached as parent_pattern + offset; `va` is a base-relative absolute (data globals, which have no code pattern). `status`: ok = pattern/anchor resolvable in the current corpus; va = base-relative only; unverified = documented in an older corpus, not yet re-confirmed against the shipped pattern DB.

symbols.name: MagicalObject_SpawnAllObjects
symbols.note: Spawns every magical-object resource into the runtime pool. Inlined inside FUN_1402586f0; runs once at boot during InitialLoading. Loader post-detours this to inject custom items.

symbols.name: MagicalObject_SpawnContainingFunc
symbols.note: Outer function (1283 bytes) that contains the inlined SpawnAllObjects entry at +0x70. This is the pattern-resolvable anchor.

symbols.name: InitialLoading_SpawnMagicalObjects
symbols.note: Boot 'InitialLoading - MagicalObject SpawnAllObjects' caller that invokes SpawnAllObjects(g_MagicalObjectPool, ...). Address from an older corpus; re-confirm against current pattern DB.

symbols.name: MagicalObjectPool_SourceLookup
symbols.signature: void*(void* pool, void* out, void* id)
symbols.note: Source-list lookup into the magical-object pool. Scans pool source array (*pool, count at pool[1]) for the entry whose GUID matches *id/id[1]; writes the found source into *out and returns out. Re-confirmed in Ghidra 2026-06-07 (decompile @0x1402590c0 matches: 3 args, calls Entity_FindMagicalObjectComponent).

symbols.name: Resource_LookupByPath
symbols.signature: void*(const char* decoded_path, void*, void*, void*)
symbols.note: Canonical resource-by-path hashmap lookup. RCX = decoded path; returns EntityResource* (0 if not loaded). Only resolves paths registered in UsedRscList/cache.

symbols.name: Definitions_LoadGroup
symbols.note: Loads the 'Definitions' group / VersionDefinition manifest (triggers loading the curated content list). Address from older corpus.

symbols.name: Vector_Grow
symbols.signature: void(void* vec, void* /*dead RDX*/, uint32_t new_cap /*R8*/)
symbols.note: Engine vector growth helper. new_cap is the 3rd arg (R8); RDX is dead. Used when force-pushing nodes into engine collections.

symbols.name: MagicalObjectPool_Grow
symbols.signature: void(void* pool_plus_0x10, uint32_t count, uint32_t by)
symbols.note: Grows the runtime array at pool+0x10 before storing a spawned component. Re-confirmed resolvable in Ghidra 2026-06-07 (@0x1401550d0). Sibling of the generic Vector_Grow.

symbols.name: Entity_AllocInstance
symbols.note: Free-list instance allocator: pops a node from the allocator's free list (or constructs one via vtable+0x50 when empty), links it into the live list, returns the instance ptr. Single arg = the allocator/pool struct (e.g. resource+0x18). Re-confirmed in Ghidra 2026-06-07 (decompile @0x14068fe90: 1 arg, returns node).

symbols.name: Entity_FindMagicalObjectComponent
symbols.note: Finds the magical-object component in a spawned entity instance; pass g_MagicalObjectComponentMeta as arg2. Re-confirmed in Ghidra 2026-06-07 (called by MagicalObjectPool_SourceLookup with DAT_141470038 as the meta arg). Sibling of the generic Entity_FindComponentByType.

symbols.name: Entity_FindComponentByType
symbols.note: Generic find-sub-component-by-type on a spawner game object.

symbols.name: SkinRoster_Build
symbols.note: Skin-pack roster builder. Selectable-skin count (9) is baked into its loop; a new selectable skin needs a detour here, not pure data.

symbols.name: SkinGrid_Populate
symbols.note: Writes the visible skin roster into the grid; filter compares each node to 3. Loader post-detours this to force-push a custom node.

symbols.name: Reward_InitAllRewards
symbols.note: _InitAllRewards (7351 bytes): reward-type registrar. The actual reward roller is a sibling. oCDtRewardDefinition is the entity class.

symbols.name: Netcode_PeerStateTick
symbols.note: Per-peer connection-state tick (peer conn-state enum at peer+0xCC; 3=connected). Reconnect-window lever hooks here. Address from netcode corpus.

symbols.name: Netcode_DropPeer
symbols.note: Drops a peer after the reconnect window (default 60s) elapses. Address from netcode corpus.

symbols.name: Netcode_Channel_LookupById
symbols.signature: iter*(void* channel_map, iter* out, uint32_t* event_id)
symbols.note: Event-channel map FIND-OR-CREATE keyed by interned event id (SwissTable-style SIMD probe; hash = id * 0xde5fb9d2630458e9 folded). On miss mallocs a 0x20 channel node { u32 event_id @+0x00; sub** array @+0x08; u32 count @+0x10; u32 cap @+0x14; sub* in_dispatch_cursor @+0x18 } and inserts it. Writes an iterator {ctrl_slot, value_slot, inserted_flag} into out and returns out. Generic template fn (~200 callers); the named-event channel maps live at <dispatcher>+0x28, e.g. entity+0x500 (= entity+0x4d8 dispatcher) and world+0x368. Verified in Ghidra 2026-06-11; promoted from events corpus.

symbols.name: Netcode_Channel_Unsubscribe
symbols.note: REMOVE a subscription from a channel node (the events corpus mislabeled this 'Subscribe' — verified 2026-06-11 it is the unsubscribe). arg1 = channel_node+0x08 (the {array,count|cap,cursor} triple), arg2 = address of the holder's subscription-handle slot. Reads the sub's index at sub+0x18, swap-removes it from the array, fixes the swapped sub's index, releases the sub (FUN_14051eb00) and nulls the slot. If the sub being removed IS the one currently mid-dispatch (node+0x18 cursor) it just sets the cursor to -1 and lets NamedEvent_Dispatch finish the removal. The real subscribe is inlined per call-site (alloc sub FUN_140219dc0 + store functor FUN_14051b580 + append), so there is no single subscribe symbol.

symbols.name: String_Assign
symbols.note: Engine string-assign into a slot from a (ptr,len) StringDesc.

symbols.name: Entry_Ctor
symbols.note: Constructs an entry/array element used by the spawn path.

symbols.name: Format_String
symbols.note: printf-style format/string builder (e.g. 'Is Hero liked by {}', 'Chance to give {} MO'). Useful xref anchor for locating gameplay logic by its format literal.

symbols.name: Analytics_SubmitNamedEvent
symbols.signature: void(void* analytics_mgr, void* payload_kv, StringDesc* event_name, char has_run_ctx)
symbols.note: CENTRAL TELEMETRY SINK. ~37 gameplay callers funnel named analytics events through here (run_end, enemy_killed, matchmaking_start, level_up_reach, level_up_book, ...), each building a key-value payload then submitting as JSON (projectId 'passtech-ravenswatch') to Passtech's analytics backend over an authenticated HTTP POST. param_3 is a StringDesc { const char* ptr @+0x0; uint32 len|0x80000000 @+0x8 } holding the event name. The loader 'firehose' detour (hook_events.cpp::install_analytics_firehose) reads that name and re-publishes it to the Lua bus by its raw name, so ONE hook exposes every named event to mods (R.on('enemy_killed', cb)) and survives the game adding new event names. OBSERVATION-GRADE: these fire AFTER the gameplay action and carry analytics KV, not live entity handles — good for 'when X happens do Y' triggers, not for mutating the actor. For entity-context gameplay events (damage, give-item) see the oCGameNamedEvent bus — mapped: NamedEvent_Dispatch is the single hook point (R.on('gameplay:<NAME>'), docs/_re/kinds/events-bus.md). Skips 'run_end' to avoid double-firing the typed Event_RunEnd table hook.

symbols.name: NamedEvent_Dispatch
symbols.note: THE oCGameNamedEvent bus dispatch — one detour here exposes every entity-context gameplay event (NETWORK_DAMAGE, GIVE_MAGICAL_OBJECT, GAIN_REROLL, ...) with a live payload. dispatcher = the NamedEventDispatcher sub-object (entity+0x4d8 for entity events; world+0x340 for world events; channel map at dispatcher+0x28, dispatch queue at +0x00..0x18, re-entrancy guard at +0x60). Clones the event (vcall ev+0x18), enqueues the clone, then (unless re-entrant) drains the queue: find-only channel lookup (NamedEvent_ChannelMap_Find) by *(u32*)(ev+0x30), iterates the node's sub array setting the node+0x18 cursor, invokes (*(sub+0x10))(ev, sub) per subscriber, handles mid-dispatch self-unsubscribe (cursor == -1), erases empty channels, deletes the clone (NamedEvent_Delete). Event header (all classes): vft @+0x00, u32 2 @+0x08, name String {char* @+0x20, u32 cap|0x80000000 @+0x28, u32 len @+0x2c}, u32 interned id @+0x30 — so the hook reads the PLAINTEXT name straight off the event. Loader detour: hook_events.cpp::install_gameplay_bus (RSMM_ENABLE_GAMEPLAY_EVENTS=1), published as R.on('gameplay:<NAME>'). Also the local-emit primitive: construct an event and call this directly (the give-MO path in FUN_140397190 does exactly that).

symbols.name: NamedEvent_ChannelMap_Find
symbols.signature: iter*(void* channel_map, iter* out, uint32_t* event_id)
symbols.note: Find-only sibling of Netcode_Channel_LookupById (no insert on miss; miss = iterator at map end). Used by NamedEvent_Dispatch to locate the channel node for an event id.

symbols.name: NamedEvent_HeroSubscribeAll
symbols.note: Hero post-spawn/post-load init + named-event subscription setup. Single-arg void(hero) (verified by disasm: only RCX is read; RDX/R8/XMM are overwritten before use, so safe to re-call as (void*)). PROLOGUE re-syncs the hero's own HP from the HUD mirror: reads f32 at *(hero+0x1d80) and writes it to BOTH hero+0x15cc (max) and hero+0x15c8 (cur) — so param_1 is the hero HP-CARRIER, the same object Entity_ModifyHealth mutates. Then runs 26+ inlined subscribes registering hero handler slots hero+0x2fa..0x321 (qword indices) on the entity channel map (entity+0x500) and the world map (world+0x368); catalog of every (id global, name, slot) pair in docs/_re/kinds/events-bus.md — includes GIVE_MAGICAL_OBJECT -> hero+0x306. Runs ONCE at hero spawn, before the hero acts, and is hero-only (enemies have no HUD mirror) — so the loader hooks it read-only as the INSTANT, authoritative hero-capture source (install_hero_capture, hook_events.cpp), eliminating the old capture-on-first-heal/pickup latency. The events corpus called this 'the give-handler'; it is the subscription setup (the give handler proper is the functor it registers for slot 0x306).

symbols.name: NamedEvent_HeroUnsubscribeAll
symbols.note: Hero teardown twin of NamedEvent_HeroSubscribeAll: walks the same (id global, slot) pairs and calls Netcode_Channel_Unsubscribe on each. Easiest place to read the full hero event catalog (one lookup+unsubscribe pair per event).

symbols.name: NamedEvent_GiveMagicalObject_Ctor
symbols.note: In-place ctor of NamedEventGiveMagicalObject (object size 0x60): sets vft chain (oCGameNamedEvent -> ...Network -> NamedEventGiveMagicalObject), u32 2 @+0x08, name 'GIVE_MAGICAL_OBJECT' @+0x20 (non-owned literal, flag 0x80000000 @+0x28), interned id @+0x30, peer -1 @+0x38, 0 @+0x40, -1 @+0x48, payload zeroed: MO definition GUID @+0x50/+0x58 (16 bytes, from MagicalObjectDefinition+0x88). Fill the GUID then call NamedEvent_Dispatch(entity+0x4d8, ev) to give an item locally. NOTE: pattern is non-unique (match_index 11/13 — small ctor template); resolver picks by rank, fragile across game updates, fn_verify guards misresolution.

symbols.name: NamedEvent_Delete
symbols.note: Virtual delete for bus objects: vcall ev+0x10 = scalar dtor with free flag 1 (frees on the GAME heap). Dispatch uses it on the queued clone. Only call on game-heap objects — never on loader-owned/static event buffers (their dtor-free would cross heaps).

symbols.name: NamedEvent_Id_FromCrc
symbols.note: Interned event-id derivation: id = crc32 over the 8 bytes of (ns, name_crc) interleaved byte-wise (standard reflected crc32 table). Event names are interned at static-init as id = NamedEvent_Id_FromCrc(0, crc32(name)) — so the loader can derive the id for ANY event name at runtime (used by the Lua gameplay-emit primitive).

symbols.name: NamedEvent_NetSend
symbols.note: Network leg of the bus: on the owning peer stamps ev+0x38 with the local session id and forwards to NamedEvent_NetSendToPeer; replicated events (oCGameNamedEventNetwork subclasses) reach remote entities this way. net_event_cpnt = entity component class-id 0x154fce5c (looked up via FUN_1403124b0(entity), component map at entity+0x5e8).

symbols.name: NamedEvent_NetSendToPeer
symbols.signature: void(void* net_event_cpnt, oCGameNamedEvent* ev, uint64_t* peer_session)
symbols.note: Wraps the event in an oCNamedEventNetworkMessage {vft 0x140f96b28, msg class id 0x157f6854, ev*} and unicasts it via the session vcall +0xc0 (skips if target session == local). Receive side deserializes via the message's Serialize (FUN_14085dec0; allocates the event from the class registry DAT_14146b2d8 by serialized class index, restores ev+0x30) and dispatches into the target entity's NamedEvent_Dispatch.

symbols.name: NamedEvent_EmitNetworkDamageFromHit
symbols.note: Reference emitter for NETWORK_DAMAGE: stack-builds the full oCGameNamedEventNetworkDamage (size 0x110) — header as usual, f32 value @+0x40, source net-id @+0x48 (FUN_140726330), embedded oCEntityHitData @+0x50 (vft @+0x50, target entity* @+0x60 refcounted, hit floats/vectors +0x68..0xbc, u64s @+0xc0/0xc8/0xd0, u16 @+0xd8, ptr @+0xe0, instigator entity* @+0xf0 refcounted, flag byte @+0x100) — then sends via NamedEvent_NetSend. Best anchor for decoding the damage payload. For self/non-networked targets it applies locally via Entity_DispatchHit instead of (or alongside) the net send.

symbols.name: Entity_DispatchHit
symbols.note: LOCAL damage/hit application — the enemy-damage counterpart to Entity_ModifyHealth (which is hero-only). param_1 = the TARGET entity; its hit component lives inline (mutex @+0x498, hit-handler list {base @+0x4b0, count @+0x4b8}, reentrancy guard @+0x4c0, pending-hit array {base @+0x4c8, count @+0x4d0, cap @+0x4d4}). param_2 = a fully-built oCEntityHitData (~0xb0 bytes: vft @+0x0, source/instigator entity* @+0x10, copied hit floats/vectors @+0x18..0x90, target entity* @+0xa0; the two entity ptrs are accessed through their vtables, so must be live oCEntity handles). When no hit handler is mid-dispatch it runs the target's hit handlers immediately, otherwise it memcpy-queues a 0xb0 hit-data copy into the pending array. Called by NamedEvent_EmitNetworkDamageFromHit for self/non-networked targets. ENEMY-DAMAGE BLOCKER: there is no low-arity 'damage entity by amount' primitive — both this and the network path require constructing a complete oCEntityHitData with valid source+target handles, which is the real work item for offensive tier-2. Helpers: FUN_1403124b0(entity)=net/replication state (returns obj whose +0x130 byte = is-remote flag), FUN_140726330(entity)=source net-id.

symbols.name: Entity_GetNetComponent
symbols.note: SwissTable/F14 component-map lookup on an entity for the fixed type-id 0x154fce5c (the net/replication component). Probes the entity's component map (control bytes @entity+0x5e8, slots @entity+0x5f0, bucket mask @entity+0x600) and returns the component pointer, or 0 if the entity has none (e.g. single-player / non-replicated). The returned component's byte @+0x130 is the local/remote AUTHORITY flag: 0 = locally controlled (this client owns the entity and emits its NETWORK_DAMAGE), nonzero = remotely controlled (apply received state, don't emit). Both hit paths (NamedEvent_EmitNetworkDamageFromHit, the attack resolver FUN_1403dc780) gate network emit on this flag. NOTE: it dereferences the component map unconditionally, so only call on a known-valid entity. Pattern is multi-match (index 3/6, 128-byte sig) — fn_verify-guarded. Relevant to local-vs-remote hero disambiguation in co-op, though hero-capture already pins the local player via the HUD-mirror requirement (only the local player has one).

symbols.name: Entity_ResolveAttackHits
symbols.signature: float(void* attacker, uint hitDefIndex, TargetList* targets, float damageMul, float baseDamage)
symbols.note: Attack-resolution / multi-target hit applier — the real producer that builds an oCEntityHitData per target and calls Entity_DispatchHit. param_1 = attacker context (its hit-def array @+0xd8, entity @+0x8); param_2 = index into that hit-def array; param_3 = target list {count @+0x0, entity** @+0x8}; param_4 = damage multiplier; param_5 = base damage (if <=0, pulled from the hit-def's value object). Per target it: allocs a hit handle (FUN_140214f30, released by NamedEvent_Delete), stack-builds the 0xb0 oCEntityHitData (vft=oCEntityHitData_vftable, 4 constant template vectors from 0x140fc6c10/6c50/6e70/7240, hit-value obj* whose +0x8 = the damage, attacker @ a slot, target position from target.vtable[+0x48], source net-id via Entity_GetNetComponent), then Entity_DispatchHit(target, hitData). THE ENEMY-DAMAGE ENTRY POINT: there is no standalone oCEntityHitData ctor — construction is inlined here and needs a real attacker hit-def, so synthesizing a hit from nothing is impractical. The viable mod path is to HOOK this and AMPLIFY/redirect: scale the hit-value damage (*(hitval+0x8)) or swap the target list. See docs/_re/kinds/enemy-damage.md.

symbols.name: oCEntityHitData_vftable
symbols.note: vftable of oCEntityHitData (the ~0xb0-byte hit descriptor passed to Entity_DispatchHit / embedded in oCGameNamedEventNetworkDamage). Layout (offsets from the struct base): vft @+0x0, hit handle/id @+0x8, source/instigator entity* @+0x10 (vtable-accessed, refcounted), float/vector block @+0x18..0x90 (positions/normals/direction — defaults copied from 0x140fc6c10/0x140fc6c50/0x140fc6e70/0x140fc7240), u16 flags @+0x88, ptr @+0x90, target entity* @+0xa0 (vtable-accessed, refcounted). Built inline by Entity_ResolveAttackHits; no separate constructor exists.

symbols.name: HeroController_Ctor
symbols.note: Constructor of oCDtEntityCpntHeroController — THE object R.entity/R.combat capture (the 'hero pointer'); it is the hero CONTROLLER COMPONENT, not the top-level entity. Confirms the capture layout: vftable @+0x0; current HP f32 @+0x15c8, max HP @+0x15cc, missing-health ratio @+0x15d0 (default 1.0f), ratio divisor @+0x15d4 (default 0.5f); HUD HP-mirror pointer @+0x1d80 (index 0x3b0) is built here via HeroController_HudMirror_Ctor (FUN_1403b2f20) — this is why +0x1d80 is the local-hero discriminator. Component size ~0x1e40. ARCHITECTURE: the hero's stats are oe::EntityCpntValueSignal<bool|int|float|oCVec3> reactive-signal sub-components (dozens of them) — a change to a signal fires on the gameplay bus, which is why stat changes are observable as named events. HP is additionally MIRRORED to the plain f32 at +0x15c8 for the hot path, which is exactly why R.combat can read/write it directly while most other stats live inside signal objects (no fixed plain-float offset). A 10-slot ability/input config block of int tags sits at +0x1fc..+0x220 = {0,1,1,1,2,1,1,1,1,3}.

symbols.name: HeroController_HudMirror_Ctor
symbols.note: Builds the hero's HUD HP-mirror object whose pointer is stored at hero+0x1d80 by HeroController_Ctor. Entity_ModifyHealth writes new HP to *(*(hero+0x1d80)) and the HUD reads it; only the local player gets one, so its presence is the local-hero discriminator used by hero_plausible.

symbols.name: g_MagicalObjectPool
symbols.note: Magical-object pool global pointer. Layout at *ptr: +0x0 source array (MagicalObjectDefinition*[]), +0x8 source count, +0x10 runtime array, +0x18 runtime count. Each source def carries its identity GUID at def+0x88/+0x90 — the value MagicalObjectPool_SourceLookup matches. GIVE-ITEM RECIPE (proven in-game 2026-06-12): read a source def's +0x88/+0x90 GUID, build a GIVE_MAGICAL_OBJECT event (NamedEvent_GiveMagicalObject_Ctor), write that GUID to ev+0x50/+0x58, NamedEvent_Dispatch(hero+0x4d8, ev) — the give handler (FUN_1403a7ba0) resolves the def via SourceLookup and grants the item straight to inventory (no world orb), then fires SPAWN_MO at the hero.

symbols.name: g_GameOptions
symbols.note: Game-options registry singleton pointer (set by the options ctor FUN_1401c99f0; *ptr = the options object). Holds every persisted GameOption inline: volumes, screen shake, plus debug/cheat toggles (Forced seed, Show enemy debug info, Show hourglass debug info, Force epilogue, Force end credits, Sectorize enemy camps, Show damage and healing numbers, ...). Each option is a 0x30-byte struct: +0x0 vftable, +0x8 u32 hashed id, +0x10 name char*, +0x18 flags, +0x28 CURRENT VALUE (bool=u8, uint/int/float=u32), +0x2c default. Consumers hold a resolved option pointer and read the inline +0x28 field (the hashed id is a baked immediate only in the ctor, never at read sites), so writing +0x28 at runtime is authoritative. Exposed via R.options.get/set in rsmm.lua. PROVEN in-game 2026-06-13: write-read-back round-trips stick (Forced seed 0->1337) and 'Show enemy debug info' = true renders per-enemy + hero HP bars — i.e. that debug feature is NOT double-gated by g_bEnableDebug. Some other pure-debug toggles might still be gated by g_bEnableDebug (a runtime-built CRC cvar — value not statically resolvable); test per-option in-game.

symbols.name: Entity_ModifyHealth
symbols.signature: void(oCEntity* hero, float delta, oCCustomFlagList* sourceTags)
symbols.note: Core HP-modification routine on the hero CHARACTER object (delta>0 heals, delta<0 damages) — the engine's own heal/damage primitive, with clamping, the UI mirror write, analytics submit, and the gained/lost named-event cascade. IMPORTANT: hero is NOT the bus dispatcher and NOT dispatcher-0x4d8 (that was a wrong guess that crashed; the dispatcher and the hero character are separate heap objects). The hero is baked into each event subscription as the handler's param_1 — capture it by hooking a hero-bound handler (Entity_GainHealthHandler / Entity_GiveHandler, both param_1=hero, pointer-only sigs). HERO HEALTH LAYOUT: current HP f32 @hero+0x15c8, max HP f32 @hero+0x15cc, missing-health ratio @+0x15d0, UI/display mirror pointer @hero+0x1d80 (the routine writes new HP to both +0x15c8 and *(*(hero+0x1d80))). HERO-ONLY — DO NOT call on enemies: param_1+0x1d80 (the HUD mirror) is dereferenced UNCONDITIONALLY for any nonzero delta (`**(param_1+0x1d80)=newHP`, plus `*(*(param_1+0x1d80)+0x10)` on heal and a +0x1db0 secondary mirror) — an enemy/non-player entity has no HUD mirror there, so calling this on one access-violates. Enemy damage must use a different path (the hit-data network-damage event NamedEvent_EmitNetworkDamageFromHit / oCGameNamedEventNetworkDamage, which carries a full oCEntityHitData), NOT this routine. R.combat is therefore correctly hero-scoped. sourceTags = an oCCustomFlagList ctx (vftable @va 0x140efc320, then {list=0, count=0}); an EMPTY flag list {vftable,0,0} is accepted. Verified by decompiling the inbound GAIN_HEALTH handler FUN_1403993f0, which calls this twice: damage = ModifyHealth(hero, -amt, tags{'Damage'}), heal = ModifyHealth(hero, +amt, tags). Exposed via R.entity / R.combat in rsmm.lua. Float arg requires the (ptr,float,ptr) prototype added to fn_call.cpp.

symbols.name: Entity_GainHealthHandler
symbols.signature: void(oCEntity* hero, void* a2, void* valueCtx)
symbols.note: Inbound GAIN_HEALTH / HEALTH_MODIFICATION handler bound to the hero. param_1 = the hero character (HP@+0x15c8); reads it directly and calls Entity_ModifyHealth(hero, ...). Pointer-only args (safe to hook). Hooked read-only by R.entity (rsmm.lua) to CAPTURE the live hero pointer the first time the hero heals/regens.

symbols.name: Entity_GiveHandler
symbols.note: Inbound GIVE_MAGICAL_OBJECT handler. param_1 = hero, param_2 = the give event; resolves the MO def via MagicalObjectPool_SourceLookup (FUN_1402590c0 on g_MagicalObjectPool) then grants via FUN_140397190(hero, def, ...). Pointer-only args (safe to hook). Also hooked read-only by R.entity to capture the hero pointer on item pickup/grant.

symbols.name: oCCustomFlagList_vftable
symbols.note: vftable of oCCustomFlagList. An empty list is the 0x18-byte struct { vftable @+0x0, list ptr @+0x8 = 0, u64 count @+0x10 = 0 } — used as the sourceTags ctx arg to Entity_ModifyHealth. Build it in scratch and rebase the vftable by the live module base.

symbols.name: Netcode_EntityReplSetup
symbols.note: Per-entity replication setup; reads the authority role = *(netmgr+0xf8) where netmgr = *(replContext+0x10), with 1 = client/non-master. The host-migration research lever: hook to observe role on host vs client, optionally overwrite it. Exposed via R.net.on_repl_setup (offsets SDK-internal). See docs/_re/MULTIPLAYER.md and [[multiplayer-netcode]].

symbols.name: g_RosterManager
symbols.note: Manager pointer global (relocated by the live image base) walked by the skin-grid populate path.

symbols.name: g_MagicalObjectComponentMeta
symbols.note: oCMetaClass* for the magical-object component; passed to Entity_FindMagicalObjectComponent.

symbols.name: Library_EnemyDefinition_vftable
symbols.note: vftable of oCTLibrary<oCDtEnemyDefinition> singleton.

symbols.name: Library_EnemyTribeDefinition_vftable
symbols.note: vftable of oCTLibrary<oCDtEnemyTribeDefinition> singleton.

symbols.name: Library_EnemyCampTierDefinition_vftable
symbols.note: vftable of oCTLibrary<oCDtEnemyCampTierDefinition> singleton.

symbols.name: Library_EnemyCampDifficultyDefinition_vftable
symbols.note: vftable of oCTLibrary<oCDtEnemyCampDifficultyDefinition> singleton.

symbols.name: Library_DreamShardDefinition_vftable
symbols.note: vftable of oCTLibrary<oCDtDreamShardDefinition> singleton.

symbols.name: Library_AchievementDefinition_vftable

payload.name: level
payload.note: new hero level; emitter stores (int)*arg at ctx+0xCC (verified in Ghidra 2026-06-05)

symbols.note: Emitter whose body references the 'level_up_reach' string (xref 0x1401f64a4). void(ctx, float* level): stores (int)*level at ctx+0xCC. Loader post-detours it to publish 'level_up' with {level} via R.on('level_up', cb).

symbols.name: Event_RunEnd
symbols.note: Emitter whose body references the 'run_end' string (xref 0x1401f5347). Loader post-detours it to publish the 'run_end' Lua event via R.on('run_end', cb).

symbols.name: EnemyDef_PostLoad
symbols.note: oCDtEnemyDefinition vftable+0x90 post-deserialize callback. Resolves the tribe typed-ref block at +0x2e8 (resolved ptr -> +0x318) via ResourceRef_Resolve, then SELF-REGISTERS into the tribe's runtime roster vector (tribe+0x2b8 data / +0x2c0 count, push_back via FUN_1401550d0) and folds min/max spawn-tier aggregates into tribe+0x2c8/+0x2cc/+0x2d0. Finally registers the instance in the class registry (Registry_RegisterInstance). THE tribe-roster writer: any loaded enemy def with a resolvable tribe_ref becomes a spawn candidate automatically.

symbols.name: EnemyTribeDef_PostLoad
symbols.note: oCDtEnemyTribeDefinition vftable+0x90 post-deserialize callback. Resolves each 0x38-stride typed-ref entry of the COOKED entry vector at +0x2a0/+0x2a8 (empty in all 25 vanilla tribes), then registers in the class registry. Does NOT write the runtime roster (+0x2b8) - enemies self-register there via EnemyDef_PostLoad.

symbols.name: InitialLoading_LoadAllDefinitions
symbols.note: Boot stage 'InitialLoading - Load all definitions'. Loads Versions/LiveOps5.versiondef.ot first, then directory-scans the 'Definitions' folder of the resource FS (index = UsedRscList.ot) and loads EVERY definition file found except 7 excluded classes (tribe class among them; tribes load lazily when an enemy tribe_ref resolves). This is why a custom .enemydef.ot registered in UsedRscList loads at boot with no further reference needed.

symbols.name: ResourceRef_Resolve
symbols.signature: void(void* refBlock, void* classDesc, void** outResolved, void* policy)
symbols.note: Generic typed resource-ref resolver. Ref block layout (0x38 bytes): {char* name, u32 hash, char* parentPath, u32 hash2, void* classDescriptor @+0x20, u8 resolved @+0x28, void* resolvedPtr @+0x30}. Resolving loads the target resource on demand.

symbols.name: Registry_RegisterInstance
symbols.note: Pushes a definition instance into the global instance list (DAT_141439de0) and its per-class registry list (via class descriptor vfunc[0] + Registry_EnumInstances). Guarded by a per-instance registration counter at +0x280.

symbols.name: Registry_EnumInstances
symbols.signature: void*(void* unused, void* out3, void** classDescPtr)
symbols.note: Registry hash-map find-or-insert keyed on *classDescPtr (callers copy the class-descriptor global into a local and pass its address). Fills out3 = {ctrl_ptr, entry_ptr, inserted_flag(u8)} and returns out3; entry = {key @+0, instance_data(void**) @+8, count(u32) @+0x10} = all live instances of the definition class. Read-side callers (e.g. camp tier selector FUN_140330db0) guard descriptor != sentinel DAT_14146fe00, falling back to the global all-instances list DAT_141439de0/+8. Used by level-load stage 3, spawn pickers, and the loader registry dump (hook_registry.cpp).

symbols.name: EnemyDefinition_ctor
symbols.note: oCDtEnemyDefinition ctor (size 0x350, UID 0x176debb7, vftable 0x140f0af80). Typed ref blocks: entity ref @+0x288 (resolved @+0x2b8), tribe ref @+0x2e8 (resolved @+0x318, class desc default @+0x308). Flag list @+0x2c0. minTier f32 @+0x2dc, tier range {u32,u32} @+0x2e0 init {0,5}, weightA @+0x320 + table @+0x328/+0x330, weightB @+0x338 + table @+0x340/+0x348.

symbols.name: EnemyTribeDefinition_ctor
symbols.note: oCDtEnemyTribeDefinition ctor (size 0x2d8, UID 0x176dc2eb, vftable 0x140efea30). Tribe flag list @+0x288; cooked entry vector @+0x2a0/+0x2a8; runtime roster {data,count} @+0x2b8/+0x2c0 (written only by EnemyDef_PostLoad); tier aggregates @+0x2c8 (min, init FLT_MAX) /+0x2cc (max, init -FLT_MAX) /+0x2d0 (maxTierHi u32).

symbols.name: EnemyCamp_TierSelector
symbols.note: Camp generation: picks tribes (EnemyCamp_TribeEntryBuilder), then per tribe entry copies the tribe runtime roster (+0x2b8/+0x2c0) as the candidate vector, trims it with EnemyCamp_Stage3Filter, weighted-picks until camp power weight reached. Logs 'Min/Max power weight', 'Generation complete !'.

symbols.name: EnemyCamp_TribeEntryBuilder
symbols.signature: void(void* selector, void* specialEntry, void* outEntries, float mult)
symbols.note: Builds the camp's tribe entry list: tribe pool = map def list (mapdef+0x720 -> +0x2c0 stride 0x38) or, if absent, ALL tribes from the class registry; filters via EnemyTribeDefInternal::SearchFilter, weighted-picks tribes, precomputes per-enemy spawn counts from the tribe roster.

symbols.name: EnemyCamp_Stage3Filter
symbols.note: Trims an enemy-def candidate vector by tier range (+0x2e0), min tier (+0x2dc), flag include/exclude (+0x2c0 list), tribe whitelist (+0x318) and tier-weight tables. Only removes - never adds. (Rebase of old FUN_14030b000 notes.)

symbols.name: Enemy_RuntimeSpawnPicker
symbols.note: Spawn-time weighted picker: enumerates ALL enemy defs from the class registry (NOT the tribe roster), filters by tier/flags/allowed-tribe-ptr, weighted-random picks, lazily resolves the entity ref (+0x288 block) and appends spawn data.

symbols.name: LevelLoad_Orchestrator
symbols.note: Runs the 'Level load - *' stage chain (hero entities, barks, 'Enemies settings loading' = blocking-load of registry enemy defs filtered by map-def tribe list, map/tile defs, enemy camp generation via named event, navmesh, sectorization).

symbols.name: Registry_EnemyDefinition_desc
symbols.note: Class registry descriptor for oCDtEnemyDefinition (set by registrar FUN_14022d940; UID 0x176debb7, instance size 0x350). Enumerate instances via Registry_EnumInstances.

symbols.name: Registry_EnemyTribeDefinition_desc
symbols.note: Class registry descriptor for oCDtEnemyTribeDefinition (registrar FUN_140189410; UID 0x176dc2eb, size 0x2d8). Default descriptor for enemy tribe_ref resolution (enemy+0x308).

_event_catalog_doc: Observation events the loader republishes by raw name from the central telemetry sink (Analytics_SubmitNamedEvent). No address — the firehose detour reads the name at runtime, so any name the game adds also fires even if absent here. These are confirmed names harvested by string-xref (cluster 0x140f13a00-0x140f13f00); subscribe via R.on('<name>', cb) with RSMM_ENABLE_GAME_EVENTS=1. Shown by `rsmm symbols events`.

event_catalog.name: level_up_reach
event_catalog.note: hero reached a new level (telemetry name; the typed 'level_up' event carries {level})
